cohort_total_n_excerpt: Tea consumption data for 27,293 men were collected at baseline (between 1993 and 1998) using a validated food frequency questionnaire.
reason: The abstract reports total incident prostate cancer after prospective follow-up but provides no aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal prostate cancer analysis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: For black tea, a statistically significant positive association and trend were observed for daily intake compared with no black tea intake (HR = 1.41, 95 % CI 1.03, 1.92; p for trend <0.01)
estimate_classifications.reason: The black-tea estimate concerns overall incident prostate cancer, with no aggressive subtype specified.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There was no association between daily green tea intake and prostate cancer risk, compared with no green tea intake [hazard ratio (HR) = 1.08; 95 % confidence interval (CI) 0.79, 1.47].
estimate_classifications.reason: The green-tea estimate concerns overall incident prostate cancer, with no aggressive subtype specified.
